name: bodypart-student

cpu.note: measured as the cascade bodypart-cascade@r7-fast end to end, which is how this part is served; A5.2.3e, round 1's four blocks pooled (11,081 scored stacks, 32 and 64 workers), cold on the client (the storage server held these blocks): 5.21 h for the 544,972-stack frame. big-1 on the CPU at 32 workers, read third, ran 34.3 a second (4.42 h). Before the overlap A5.3 measured 19.5 a second (ims-a53-bp)
cpu.hardware: 64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB of memory, the archive over NFS 4.2; CPU only; nils-bodypart 0.5.0 (the overlap, its start in the workers), CPU build, torch 2.13.0

gpu.note: measured as the cascade bodypart-cascade@r7-fast end to end, which is how this part is served; A5.2.3e's primary run, big-1 (25,814 stacks over whole sessions, 25,208 scored), the storage server's first read, cold: 1.29 h for the frame as one container, 1.31 h in 28 parts. Cold, the storage server's file rate holds it (about 1,000 files a second)
gpu.hardware: 64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB of memory, the archive over NFS 4.2, card: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB, sm_120) under the lease; S1 on the card, 64 workers; nils-bodypart 0.5.0 (the overlap, its start in the workers), card build, torch 2.13.0

limits: A part of bodypart-cascade@r7-fast: its answers are accepted only where D3 says so, and the certified reader answers the rest
Trained on patient pixels: a site model, never exported, never in a release
A stack without registry geometry or a readable slot-0 slice goes to the planes stages
Its training set holds stacks of two samples sealed since (final-cert-2-a and -b, sealed 2026-10-04, the day before it trained); see the handover

params.loss: squared error of log(p + 1e-6) plus the KL divergence against the certified encoder's six probabilities
params.network: the few-slice study's student: EfficientNet-B0 slice encoder, slice and stack geometry tokens, attention pooling, six log-probabilities
params.numerics: fp32 on the CPU and on the card, TF32 off

tested.note: root mean square log-probability error 0.52; the student is judged only through the cascade, whose card carries the certificate
tested.claim: val top-class agreement with the certified encoder (round 2)

tested.note: 5,308 accepted, 2 fine and 2 coarse disagreements with the stored answers
tested.claim: stage 1 (S1 with D3 at 0.99) on dev B: accepted share
S1 alone on the CPU in the run's main process, 32 threads (A5.3, block 4, its S1 phase)

equivalence.set: round 1's 3,000 card stacks of the screen, over whole studies (3,213 stacks, 3,146 scored): A5.2.3a (b), registered
equivalence.note: as the cascade's stage 1: every stage decision equal on the CPU and on the card; every effective outcome of both modes, every stage decision and every top label equal, every calibrated probability within 0.001. Also class I card against CPU on round 1's four blocks (A5.2.3d, ims-a523d-bp) and, descriptively, on big-1 (A5.2.3e, ims-a523e-bp: 658 of 25,000 tables differ in their bytes, the student's probabilities at most 1e-6 apart and D3's score at most 0.026, every decision the same)

intended_use: The first stage of bodypart-cascade@r7-fast: the certified encoder's six probabilities predicted from one native slice and the registry's geometry, read by the certified head; never served alone
